reasoning: Round 2. Kept the approved driver set (Kilian 2026-11-02) unchanged; my view enters through the legs, the multiple and the scenarios. Supervisor findings acted on: (1) SBC basis: round 1 labelled the set SBC-costed but applied a 23.2x SBC-costed multiple to the engine's ex-SBC EPS (+9% overstatement); I re-derived the peer median on the SBC-costed basis (Viavi Ex.99.1 confirms non-GAAP ex-SBC, FY26 SBC $0.23/sh, so 18.8x -> 21.5x; Ralliant adjusted EPS keeps SBC), set the exit at 23.34x costed by k=0.8 and converted it to the engine's ex-SBC EPS with my build's own ratio 14.71/16.12 = 0.9126; (2) FTV is segment-only after the Ralliant spin; RAL (Tektronix) replaces it, median 23.75x; (3) print date is 2026-11-19 (company release, opened), not 11-17; (4) post-horizon China risk now sits in the multiple too: net -0.4 turn (digestion 0.35 x -2, China 0.15 x -1.5, 3.2T/6G 0.35 x +1.5); I keep -2 not -3 turns for digestion because my 30% mid-cycle leg already prices margin reversion, so I differ from the supervisor's -0.75. Alternative-lane evidence: LightCounting July 2026 (opened) sees a correction 'of some kind' as more likely and warns double ordering 'has never ended well', but a soft landing in 2027-28 if capex growth slows gradually, supporting the median path with a fat left tail; Advantest and Anritsu (src 14-15) confirm AI test demand into CY27. Build: horizon ex-SBC EPS $16.12 (costed $14.71) is ~2% above MarketScreener FY28 $14.37 on a costed basis and ~10% above Zacks FY28 $13.37 (1 est., SBC-expensed), because the approved set is above the Street on revenue (FY28 9,334 vs 8,927) and margin. Research target (12m) $322.91 (+6.4%): P/E leg $337.62 (w 0.7) and mid-cycle leg $288.6 (w 0.3). Downside case $183.54 (P10: optics digestion + China -50% + margins -5pt + 5 turns) and upside case $448.2 (P90), left tail fatter, consistent with 45% realized vol. Research limits: X/Reddit not reachable; in-lane share below 60% because filings and peer releases were needed to settle the SBC basis.

drivers.label: Wireline revenue as a share of the AI-cluster Ethernet optics market
drivers.source: Market: LightCounting AI-cluster Ethernet optics, CY2025 $16.5B (Jan 2026 forecast quoted in POET Technologies FY2025 20-F), +120% 2026 and +76% 2027 (Lightwave 2026-10-08), CY2028 by LightCounting optics/capex ratio x Big-4 capex (Lightwave 2026-03-10; series as gated in driver_models/CRDO/quarterly/set.json optical_tam), CY2029 +27.1% (linear fade of growth from +30.6% in 2028 to LightCounting's +20% by 2031). Wireline: KEYS does not disclose wireline dollars; Q3 FY26 prepared remarks: "Wireline revenue exceeded wireless revenue for the first time this quarter" of commercial communications $1,006M (https://s22.q4cdn.com/444849635/files/doc_earnings/2026/q3/transcript/Q3-FY2026-Prepared-Remarks.pdf); Q3 FY26 call: wireline roughly two-thirds R&D, one-third manufacturing (Motley Fool transcript 2026-08-25).
drivers.derivation: Wireline quarterly estimates (flag: not disclosed): FY25 229/257/290/310 (=1,086; share of CC rising 40->47%, wireline grew double digits FY25 per Q4 FY25 remarks), FY26 358/428/520 (Q3 > wireless 486) and Q4 585 (FY26 1,891). FY growth = 1/3 x market growth (manufacturing test scales with units) + 2/3 x R&D growth (estimate +25% FY27, +15% FY28, +10% FY29; no source, the main judgment): FY27 +42.0% -> 2,685, FY28 +20.2% -> 3,228, FY29 +15.7% -> 3,734. Fiscal FY n paired with CY n (variant: test leads deployment by 2-3 quarters). Quarterly market = log-linear interpolation through each CY midpoint, rescaled so each FY sums to its CY total; forecast wireline quarters grow at one constant quarterly rate per year from the prior quarter so the FY totals hold (FY27 +5.6%/qtr, FY28 +4.2%/qtr, FY29 +3.4%/qtr), capture = wireline / market. Capture FY26 5.21% -> FY27 4.20%, FY28 3.87%, FY29 3.52%. Variant: slower R&D (+15/+10/+5%) gives CC 4,526/5,076/5,571. Supply constrains conversion for several quarters (CFO, Q3 FY26 call).

horizon_multiples.peer_basis: Whole-company peer median NTM P/E on the SBC-costed basis 23.75x (VIAV 21.5 converted, RAL 21.26, AME 26.0, Anritsu 28.54); own 303.5/13.06 = 23.24x; exit 23.75 x (23.24/23.75)^0.8 = 23.34x, less 0.4 turn net post-horizon risk = 22.94x costed, x 0.9126 (costed/ex-SBC horizon EPS 14.71/16.12) = 20.94x on the engine's ex-SBC EPS

custom.name: Mid-cycle normalised EPS x through-cycle P/E
custom.explanation: Horizon NTM revenue ~9,341 (driver set, FY28 9,334 + a few days of FY29) x mid-cycle non-GAAP op margin 29.0% = 2,709, less SBC 3.0% (280.5), plus interest on engine horizon net cash 1,771 x 4% = 71, x (1-14%) = 2,151 / 170.83M horizon shares = $12.58 SBC-costed EPS x 22.94x SBC-costed exit P/E = $288.6. Same SBC-costed basis on EPS and multiple (counted once). Not driver-linked.

downside.story: 10th percentile: AI-optics test digestion arrives in CY2027 (LightCounting's 'bumpy ride' case) on top of component shortages; wireline capture -35% vs the approved path, a China shock (China revenue -50%, ~-8.7% of FY27 revenue) inside the wireless -12% / electronic-industrial -15% cuts, segment margins -5pt back toward FY25 levels, P/E -5 turns to ~15.9x ex-SBC (~17.5x SBC-costed, below VIAV/RAL at ~21x), mid-cycle leg -30%.

upside.story: 90th percentile: 1.6T ramps and 3.2T R&D start pull wireline capture +30% vs the approved path, supply loosens so the backlog converts, wireless +4%, EI +6% on AI semis, margins +1.5/+1pt, P/E +5 turns to ~25.9x ex-SBC (~28.4x SBC-costed, at Anritsu 28.5x, top of the whole-company range).

model_inputs.structure_note: Approved quarterly driver set (Kilian 2026-11-02: wl_capture, wireless_rev, adg_rev, ei_rev, csg_margin, eisg_margin with constant mkt) copied unchanged; segment income = non-GAAP op income (ex-SBC). ebit_basis adjusted with SBC costed (3.0% of revenue) in FCF; the engine's P/E reads ex-SBC NOPAT, so the SBC-costed exit multiple 22.94x is converted to 20.94x (x 0.9126). Value carried by (1) horizon NTM P/E on the build's own FY2028-weighted EPS (w 0.7) and (2) a mid-cycle SBC-costed EPS x 22.94x custom leg (w 0.3, not driver-linked; per the semis playbook so peak FY28 margins do not carry all the value). No DCF leg (not a neocloud).
model_inputs.gap_note: Views on approved drivers (not changed): csg_margin 34.5% FY28-29 and eisg_margin 31% look like peak-cycle levels (FY25 26.5%/24.7%); my mid-cycle leg uses 29% instead, worth about -$15/share on the blend vs using the driver margins throughout. wl_capture path is a fair median but with a fat left tail (LightCounting July 2026: correction more likely than not, double ordering), carried in the downside case and a -0.7 turn digestion deduction. Judgment calls for Kilian: (a) mid-cycle leg weight 0.3 (0 would add ~+$15, +4.6%); (b) post-horizon net deduction -0.4 turn vs the supervisor's -0.75 (my digestion deduction is -2 not -3 turns because the mid-cycle leg already prices margin reversion; at -0.75 the target is ~$5 lower). The ~$100M Q4 component slip (QuiverQuant) is discounted as a single unattributed report and moves no number. Custom leg is a per-share number not driver-linked. Financing: none expected (net cash ~1.8B at the horizon), so no financing_events. Taiwan conflict by end-2027 at 10% on Polymarket (2026-10-16, $3.5M volume): downside tail only.

track_record.note: Only guide midpoints recorded (low=high=mid); classified vs midpoint. Approved driver set scores 10 quarters Q2 FY24-Q3 FY26: 10 of 10 above midpoint, median +2.4%. Q2 FY26 is +3.4% before the $40M IEEPA refund. Spirent closed 2025-10-15 and is inside these guides.
